summary: Updated QA, Security Auditor, Reviewer, Release Engineer, and Documentation handoff pseudocode blocks in handoff.md — each now calls findNextReadyDispatch() immediately before its final return WAIT, enabling cross-WP dispatch in multi-WP projects.

Fixed Synthesis Handoff pseudocode to return COMPLETE instead of WAIT, and updated the design note to explain that COMPLETE signals auto-handoff orchestrators that the entire project workflow is finished.

Added §13.5 documenting the findNextReadyDispatch algorithm: READY WP routing via firstActiveStage + PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP, all-terminal READY_FOR_SYNTHESIS fallback, null return when no deterministic dispatch is possible, and the self-routing design decision.
Verified that the Synthesis inline handler in workflow-handoff.ts (line 63) already returns 'COMPLETE' — no code change was required.

comments.note: All five affected pseudocode blocks (QA, Security Auditor, Reviewer, Release Engineer, Documentation) received the findNextReadyDispatch call at the correct position — after the IN_PROGRESS assigned_to check and before the terminal return WAIT.

The Synthesis inline handler in workflow-handoff.ts was confirmed to already return 'COMPLETE' (buildHandoffResponse called with 'COMPLETE' status at line 63). The pseudocode in handoff.md was the only location returning the incorrect 'WAIT' value — no code change was needed.

§13.5 includes a behaviour summary table and two design notes: the self-routing design decision (intentional, allows agents to continue on next WP without orchestrator re-poll) and the relationship to the PM handoff (findNextReadyDispatch is the lightweight variant; PM handoff adds IN_PROGRESS pipeline-stage inspection).
